svg.title: Proof. The measure recovery theorem gives equality at each tag, including for complex integrable insertions. Consequently every difference IZ λ −IZ κ equals its target difference and every tested residual has the same value. For example, if for every ε > 0 there is an original threshold beyond which |Iλ −I| < ε, the identical threshold proves the lifted assertion. Supremum bounds over any specified parameter subset are identical. Applying this argument first to the original inner index and then to the original outer index proves the iterated assertion without exchanging limits. A distributional assertion is this same argument for each allowed test function; uniformity over a test set transfers only when it was present in the original assertion. Finite coordinate sums commute with these equalities. No new majorant, compactness assertion or test class is inferred.
